newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi launches fresh attack on Italian budget.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi launches fresh attack on Italian budget.

text.p: Former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi has launched a fresh attack on the government's 1997 budget, promising that the centre-right would continue its parliamentary protest over the deficit-cutting package.

Berlusconi told reporters late on Tuesday that the centre-right Freedom Alliance would boycott votes in the upper house of parliament on controversial parts of the budget, which is designed to prepare Italy for the single European currency.
In a hard hitting news conference, he branded Prime Minister Romani Prodi's centre-left government a "regime".
"It doesn't use tanks but it has systematically taken over power," he said.

The Freedom Alliance has been especially angered by the government's request for mandatory powers within the complex budget law, which will enable it to decide policy in areas such as fiscal reform, without recourse to parliament.
The upper house (Senate) is currently examining the 1997 budget and is due to complete ratification of the bill by the end of next week.
The package has already been approved by the lower house, despite a protest walkout by the Freedom Alliance, and will have to return to the chamber for a fresh vote by year end.

Berlusconi said the Freedom Alliance would present its proposed amendments to the budget in the Senate, but would again walk out of the chamber when the time came to vote for the special powers sought by Prodi.
Prodi's coalition government has a majority in the Senate.

Berlusconi also hinted that the centre-right might actively encourage a fiscal revolt against the budget, which aims to take 61.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's deficit through a mix of tax increases, spending cuts and treasury operations.

"I don't know how long we will carry on with our display of responsibility that has so far forced us to reject invitations from citizens and associations...to (launch) a fiscal revolt," Berlusconi said.
